new_statements.quote: Ὁ τονισμός τῆς τσακωνικῆς εἶναι δυναμικός, ὅπως καί τῆς κοινῆς νέας ἑλληνικῆς καί τῶν ἄλλων νεοελληνικῶν διαλέκτων. [...] Ὁ δυν. τόνος τῆς τσακωνικῆς εἶναι κινητός καί μπορεῖ νά πέφτει σέ μιά ἀπό τίς τρεῖς (ἐφόσον ὑπάρχουν) τελευταῖες συλλαβές τῆς τονικῆς ἑνότητας. π.χ. záuma "ζάλωμα", aθrípi "ἄνθρωποι", aramú "μένω". [...] Ἡ τονική ἑνότητα στά πλαίσια τῆς ὁποίας ἀσκεῖ τή λειτουργία του ὁ δυν. τόνος συμπίπτει στήν τσακωνική μέ τή λέξη. [...] Δέν ὑπάρχει σταθερό κριτήριο πού νά προβλέπει μέ σιγουριά σέ ποιά ἀπό τίς συλλαβές τῆς λέξης πού μποροῦν νά τονιστοῦν θά πέσει ὁ τόνος.
new_statements.translation: The accent of Tsakonian is dynamic [stress], as in Standard Modern Greek and the other Modern Greek dialects. [...] The stress of Tsakonian is mobile and may fall on any one of the last three syllables (where they exist) of the accentual unit, e.g. záuma 'patch', aθrípi 'people', aramú 'I stay'. [...] The accentual unit within which stress operates coincides in Tsakonian with the word. [...] There is no fixed criterion that predicts with certainty on which of the stressable syllables of the word the stress will fall.
new_statements.citation: Charalambopoulos [Haralambopoulos], Agathoklis L. 1980. Φωνολογική ανάλυση της τσακωνικής διαλέκτου. PhD thesis, Aristotle University of Thessaloniki (Epist. Epetirida Filosofikis Scholis, Parartima 30).
new_statements.locator: Ch. 4 Προσωδία, §4.1 Δυναμικός τονισμός, p.134 (reader image/PDF page 147); secondary stress p.136 (image 149)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened the held page images,, = printed pp.134-136 of Charalambopoulos 1980, Φωνολογική ανάλυση της τσακωνικής διαλέκτου, AUTh PhD, fetched sources from the open didaktorika.gr/EKT reader, doc 2680). Page 134 is headed '4. ΠΡΟΣΩΔΙΑ / 4.1. Δυναμικός τονισμός' and the quoted sentences are there verbatim (the '[...]' marks are genuine omissions of intervening Martinet/Garde theory sentences; 'καί' before 'τῶν ἄλλων νεοελληνικῶν διαλέκτων' is a handwritten insertion on the typescript; the right margin of the scan clips a few word-final letters, e.g. 'θά πέσ[ει] ὁ τόνος', but the wording is unambiguous): stress is dynamic as in Standard Modern Greek; 'Ὁ δυν. τόνος τῆς τσακωνικῆς εἶναι κινητός κα…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress accent (not tone), lexically/morphologically determined and contrastive by position (káli 'wood' vs kalí 'good', xóra 'town' vs xorá 'green'), confined to a window of the last three syllables of the word; not predictable by any phonological rule; stress may shift within inflectional paradigms (áθropo – aθrípi, satéra – ta saterí), as in Standard Modern Greek.
new_statements.secondary_stress: p.136: 'Στήν τσακωνική ἀναπτύσσεται ἕνας δευτερεύων τόνος, ὅταν μέ τήν προσθήκη ἑνός ἐγκλιτικοῦ παραβιάζεται ὁ νόμος τῆς τρισυλλαβίας π.χ. o ámbele "τό ἀμπέλι", ἀλλά o ámbelé mi "τό ἀμπέλι μου"' — a secondary (enclitic) stress is added when an enclitic would put the stress more than three syllables from the end; otherwise no rhythmic secondary stress is described.
new_statements.exceptions: Clitics (weak pronouns mi, ndi, ni, si; possessives; prepositions apo, se, γia, me; conjunctions tse, otshi, na; particles as, θa, na; epi in periphrastic verb forms; relative pi; indefinite ena) are stressless and attach to a host; in compounds one member loses its stress (aγrielía); some normally stressed words (afú, éni) may lose stress in connected speech.
new_statements.domain_note: The accentual unit is explicitly equated with the word (plus clitics); in neutral utterances each word's stressed syllable is about equally prominent, with emphasis able to raise one. Description based on Southern Tsakonian (Tyros, Vaskina, Melana, Leonidio speakers, fieldwork 1969-1970s); author found no speakers to record in Kastanitsa/Sitaina (Northern). Deffner 1881 §11 p.43 independently states the same three-syllable limitation ('der Ton kann nicht über die drittletzte Silbe vorrücken') and conservation of the inherited Greek accent position.
new_statements.identity_note: Haralambopoulos 1980 describes Southern Tsakonian (speakers from Tyros, Vaskina, Melana, Leonidio); he reports finding no usable speakers in Kastanitsa/Sitaina (Northern Tsakonian) and does not treat Propontis Tsakonian. Glottolog tsak1248 covers all; the statement should be taken as Southern (Leonidio-Tyros) Tsakonian. Deffner 1881 is likewise based mainly on Leonidio-area speech.

sources.note: §11 'Die Betonung im Zakonischen' (pp.36-45): accent position largely as in (Doric/common) Greek with nine listed divergences; p.43: quantity is lost, the accent rules (stressed syllable long, unstressed short), and the law 'der Ton kann nicht über die drittletzte Silbe vorrücken' survives in Tsakonian as in Modern Greek; also notes a 'singing' intonation.

sources.note: Ch.4 Prosody, 4.1 (pp.134-136): Tsakonian has dynamic (stress) accent like Standard Modern Greek; stress is mobile and may fall on any of the last three syllables of the accentual unit (= the word); no criterion predicts which; position is contrastive (káli 'wood' vs kalí 'good', xóra vs xorá); secondary stress arises when an enclitic violates the three-syllable law (o ámbele vs o ámbelé mi); stress shifts within inflectional paradigms (áθropo–aθrípi).
